content: 1. Increased plasma concentrations of certain drugs, such as rosuvastatin, when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, may elevate the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Posaconazole can elevate the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Primidone reduces the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters and affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Velpatasvir is metabolized by CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4 enzymes. Drugs that induce these enzymes may significantly lower velpatasvir plasma concentrations, potentially reducing its therapeutic efficacy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Rabeprazole increases gastric pH, which reduces velpatasvir solubility and absorption. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If medically necessary, administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with food 4 hours before omeprazole 20 mg. 6. Regorafenib likely inhibits BCRP (ABCG2) transport, increasing systemic exposure to BCRP substrates. Monitor closely for toxicity. 7. Velpatasvir inhibits OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and OATP2B1 transporters, which may increase systemic exposure to drugs like repaglinide. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 8. Rifabutin and rifampin reduce sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inducing P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. St. John’s Wort significantly decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inducing P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Velpatasvir inhibits BCRP, potentially increasing systemic exposure to BCRP substrates like rosuvastatin, simvastatin, and others. Monitor closely for adverse effects, including myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 11. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting P-gp. Monitor closely and adjust dosage if necessary. 12. Tipranavir decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inducing P-gp and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Voriconazole increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Amiodarone co-administration with sofosbuvir and other HCV direct-acting antivirals has been associated with serious symptomatic bradycardia. Monitor cardiac function closely. 15. Test all patients for current or prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection before initiating HCV direct-acting antiviral therapy. HBV reactivation has been reported in HCV/HBV co-infected patients, potentially leading to fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, or death. Monitor for HBV reactivation during and after HCV treatment. 16. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir plus ribavirin is contraindicated in pregnant women and in men whose female partners are pregnant. Ribavirin carries significant teratogenic risks. 17. There is insufficient data to determine the pregnancy risk of sofosbuvir or velpatasvir. Consider the benefits of breastfeeding alongside potential risks to the infant. 18. Oral pellets of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir should not be chewed and can be mixed with non-acidic soft foods for easier administration in children under 6 years of age. Administer with food to improve tolerability. 19. Store sofosbuvir/velpatasvir tablets or pellets below 30°C (86°F) and dispense only in the original container. 20. For drugs like tenofovir DF, monitor for associated adverse reactions when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir. 21. Tepotinib increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inhibiting P-gp. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Adjust dosage if co-administration is unavoidable. 22. Vinblastine decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inducing P-gp. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Monitor for adverse effects when co-administering BCRP substrates like seladelpar or selexipag with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir. 24. Topotecan levels may increase significantly when co-administered with velpatasvir due to BCRP inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Monitor valsartan levels when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, as velpatasvir inhibits OATP transporters. 26. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases sulbactam levels by inhibiting OAT1 transporters. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 27. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases sulfazalazine levels due to BCRP inhibition. Monitor closely for pharmacologic or adverse effects. 28. Temsirolimus levels may increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust dosage if necessary. 29.
